transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the production policy review on August 25, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the rate-limit policy that gets communicated to customers, but before I do, I need each of your teams to report your release-impacting findings. So let's hear from backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I haven't updated the policy draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this is a release-impacting finding: the current draft's 100 requests per minute would break legitimate bulk-import synchronization.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from Customer Success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to be factored into our rollout timing and customer communications.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from Security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be insufficient to protect against credential-abuse attacks. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it needs to be factored into the final policy before we go to production.
transcript.speaker: A4

We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated. This is important because the current draft policy does not specify a staffed launch window, and any rollout needs to align with this available coverage.
